transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, honestly, it's just getting to be too much. What pushed me to make this appointment is that I keep starting follow-up items after audits or mentorship events with every intention of finishing them. I'll sit down at my desk, pull up the files, and I’m ready to go. My desk is right by the window, actually, which is nice because I can see the oak tree outside. The leaves are just starting to turn, which reminds me I need to get the gutters cleaned before the winter really sets in. Last year they got so backed up it caused a leak in the guest room ceiling. It was a nightmare getting a contractor out there. Anyway, I'll start these tasks, and then I find out days later that the final email, review note, or form never actually got done. It's just sitting there, half-finished.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

No, I wouldn't say I feel hopeless or anything like that. I still really like doing my normal stuff. Like, I love baking on the weekends. I actually just made a couple loaves of sourdough on Sunday. My starter is almost three years old now—I named him Dough-Joe. But anyway, I was getting ready to bake and realized I was completely out of the good parchment paper, which is just so frustrating because the store brand at the grocery down the street always burns. Last time I used it, the smoke alarm went off and it completely terrified my dog, Buster. He hates loud noises. He actually hid under the sofa for like two hours and I had to coax him out with a piece of cheese. The sharp cheddar, not the mild stuff, he's very picky for a rescue... wait, I'm sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, feeling down. No, no, my mood is honestly fine, I'm just really frustrated with falling behind on my work stuff.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things in your life, like work, home, or other responsibilities, even when there isn't a clear problem to solve?

No, not really. I mean, I worry about normal things, I guess, but I don't sit around stressing if there's no reason to. I try to just take things as they come. Like with my car—I drive a Honda CR-V, and it’s been making this weird clicking noise when I turn left. Only left, never right. It’s so strange. I told my brother about it, he used to be a mechanic before he went back to school for physical therapy. He actually just opened his own practice in Seattle, which is huge for him because he's always wanted to be his own boss. He was looking at places in Portland, but the real estate market there is just ridiculous right now. Anyway, he told me to get the CV joint checked out, so I dropped it off at the shop this morning. The guy there, Tony, he’s great. He always gives me a fair price and he has this big orange tabby cat that just sleeps on the counter. But yeah, I don't really worry about things unless there's an actual problem, like the car.
Do you ever feel restless, like you can't sit still, or find yourself fidgeting or moving around a lot when you're trying to focus or relax?

Oh, absolutely. Sitting still for a long review... it honestly feels physically uncomfortable. It's like this pressure just keeps building and building inside me until I absolutely need to stand up, walk to the printer, or just invent some reason to move. 

Speaking of the printer, our office just got one of those massive new industrial ones, but it jams if you even look at it wrong. Last week I was trying to print a quarterly report for this client—they're a landscaping company, actually. They do really beautiful work. They just redid the flower beds in front of the library downtown and planted all these gorgeous hydrangeas. I love hydrangeas, but the soil in my yard is way too alkaline, so mine always turn pink instead of that deep blue. I tried adding coffee grounds to the soil because someone on a gardening blog said it helps with the acidity, but then Buster, my dog, started digging in it and tracked mud all over the kitchen floor. It took me an hour to mop it all up. I used this new citrus cleaner, though, and it smells amazing, like real oranges, not that fake chemical scent... 

Wait, I'm sorry, I lost my train of thought. What was the question? Oh, right, being restless. Yeah, I just get this intense pressure to move when I'm supposed to be sitting at my desk.
Do you find it hard to stay focused on tasks, even when you're trying your best, like your mind drifts or you get easily distracted by things around you?

Yeah, it's really hard. I can start a long client meeting, or like, we had this AI-tool training last week, and I'll be fully engaged at first. But then after a while, my mind just slips off. I'll realize I've missed the last few minutes even though I'm still staring right at the screen. 

Which is exactly what happened during that AI training. They're trying to get us to use this new software to automate some of our auditing processes, which, honestly, I'm a little skeptical about. I mean, you really need a human eye for some of these tax discrepancies. My friend Sarah, she's an accountant too, but she works in corporate tax—she was telling me about how they tried a similar program and it completely missed a huge depreciation error on some heavy machinery. She works for a construction firm, so they have all these massive excavators and bulldozers. My nephew is obsessed with bulldozers right now. He's three. For his birthday, I got him this little yellow hard hat and a toy dump truck, and he wouldn't take the hat off all day. He even wore it to eat his cake, which was chocolate with buttercream frosting. I'm not a huge fan of buttercream, it's too sweet for me, I prefer a cream cheese frosting... 

Sorry, I'm doing it again. Um, what were we talking about? Oh, right, losing focus. Yeah, I just drift off and miss things, even when I'm trying to pay attention.
Do these difficulties with staying focused and feeling restless happen only at work, or do you notice them in other parts of your life, like at home or during leisure activities?

It's definitely not just at work. It happens at home, too. Even during things that are supposed to be relaxing, I just can't settle. Like, if I try to read a book on the couch, or even when I'm just sitting quietly waiting for my salsa class to start... I end up humming, or checking my phone, or just talking to whoever is next to me, because pure quiet just makes me feel so antsy. 

I started taking salsa classes about six months ago, actually. It's at this little studio downtown, right next to that Italian restaurant, the one with the really good garlic knots? They bake them fresh every day. The instructor, Marco, he's originally from Colombia, and he has this incredible energy. He always wears these bright, patterned shirts. Last week he had one with little flamingos all over it. Flamingos are so interesting, aren't they? The way they get their pink color from the shrimp they eat. I read this article about how some zoos have to feed them special supplements if they don't get enough of that specific algae or shrimp, otherwise they just turn white. It's wild how diet can completely change how an animal looks. It makes you wonder about human diets, you know? Like, I've been trying to cut back on dairy lately because I heard it can cause inflammation, but it's so hard when you love cheese. I bought this vegan gouda the other day, and honestly... it just tasted like wax. 

Anyway... um. What did you ask me? Oh, right, if it happens outside of work. Yes, definitely. I just can't seem to sit quietly, no matter where I am.
